correctness.rationale: A fully reconstructed Kirchhoff backward ODE gives φ_m(s)=cosh(z)/(1+m sinh(z)^2). The Poisson renewal identity yields the exact mean. Its small-r expansion proves the sharp m=1 versus m>=2 benefit; direct positive decomposition of normalized means proves strict degree monotonicity; and a sign-controlled entire power series proves uniqueness of the limiting root and convergence of every sequence of minimizers. The included standard-library script independently checks finite-difference boundary equations, renewal, and numerical constants (52 passed diagnostics). Finite tests do not substitute for proof. Domain includes all integers m>=1, lengths L>0, diffusivities D>0, and nonnegative reset rates.

value.rationale: A natural confined Brownian-search benchmark distinguishes a blind reflecting arm from a solitary reflecting-to-absorbing interval. It gives a sharp topology threshold, an exact increasing efficiency law for every branch number, and a nontrivial quantitative asymptotic cap (about 14.47%) with a unique defining root. Such a normalized network-design invariant can be compared across branched transport search geometries, unlike a routine isolated finite example. The importance is bounded to the stated model; it is not a generic graph or thermodynamic theorem.
